name: Brightline Hi-Vis Construction Shell
description:
High-visibility orange and yellow, retroreflective tape in ANSI-compliant stripes across the chest, back, and arms. The Brightline is the jacket you see on every active construction site in GLMZ — worn by the people building the elevated transit lines, maintaining the power conduit runs, and doing the physical work that keeps the megacity standing. It's a windbreaker-weight shell with a quilted vest liner that can be removed in warmer months. The fit is utilitarian and generous enough to layer over coveralls.

Brightline is a Tier 1 to 2 safety brand that sells direct to construction companies and labor cooperatives. Individual workers sometimes buy their own when site-issued jackets wear out. The jacket carries no cachet — it is purely functional — but it's an honest symbol of labor in a city that increasingly tries to make its working infrastructure invisible.
what_it_says: You work. You build things. You're not ashamed of it.
story_hooks: Someone is using stolen Brightline jackets to move through restricted construction zones undetected — and one of the real workers is being blamed.
A labor organizer has been using the hi-vis jacket as a covert signal system — specific tape patterns indicate meeting times and locations.
A Tier 5 architect was found dead in a Brightline jacket on a construction site they'd never been authorized to visit.
